card.essence: Sulphur is Hahnemann's great anti-psoric remedy, characterised by centrifugal action from within outward with elective affinity for the skin. The typical patient is lean, stoop-shouldered, dirty, and averse to bathing, with burning sensations (especially vertex and soles), weak feeble reaction, and all orifices intensely red. Particularly indicated when carefully-selected remedies fail to act or in complaints that continually relapse, it arouses the reactive powers of the organism.
card.common_name: Sublimated Sulphur; Flowers of Sulphur; Brimstone

Dirty, filthy people prone to skin affections; aversion to being washed
All orifices intensely red (lips, ears, nostrils, eyelids, anus, urethra)

Religious melancholy; averse to business, too lazy to rouse himself

The 'ragged philosopher'—untidy scholar in threadbare clothes, disordered study
Philosophical mania from sedentary life, meditation, insufficient nutrition
Tired of life, too unhappy to live

Emaciation with good appetite; atrophy of children
Constant heat on top of head (vertex)
Halo around lamp-light; black motes before eyes

Sinking feeling at stomach 11 a.m.; drinks much, eats little
Great desire for sweets; craving for alcoholic drinks (especially beer, whiskey)

Enuresis especially in scrofulous, untidy children
Menses too late, short, scanty, difficult; thick, black, acrid
Burning in chest rising to face; rattling at 11 a.m.

Offensive odor from body not removed by washing
Sleeps in cat-naps; drowsy by day, wakeful at night; unrefreshing sleep
Scrofulous, psoric, chronic diseases from suppressed eruptions
clinical: Deficient reaction; when system refuses to respond to well-selected remedy
To facilitate absorption of serous or inflammatory exudates (brain, pleura, lungs, joints)
Chronic diseases that result from suppressed eruptions (itch, eczema)
Scrofula, psora; particularly applicable after suppression of itch

Beginning treatment of chronic cases and finishing acute ones

differentials.note: Both anti-psorics for suppressed eruptions; Psorinum more chilly, hopeless, despairs of recovery; Sulphur more irritable, hopeful dreamer
Both have burning sensations; Arsenicum restless, anxious, chilly, < after midnight; Sulphur lazy, hot, < 11 a.m., better open air
Both for eczema and constipation; Graphites more chilly, cautious, indecisive; Sulphur hot, philosophical, irritable
Both for portal congestion, irritability; Nux more fastidious, chilly, worse morning; Sulphur dirty, hot, worse 11 a.m.
Both for scrofula, sweat; Calcarea chilly, fat, cautious; Sulphur hot, lean, philosophical; Calcarea complementary to Sulphur
Both worse heat, better open air; Pulsatilla mild, tearful, yielding; Sulphur selfish, irritable, dirty

cautions: Do not use indiscriminately despite its wide sphere; select on symptoms as with any remedy
Avoid in cleanly, fastidious people—seldom indicated
Not for acute psoric eruptions where suppression is recent; works best in chronic cases
Give single dose at new moon in menorrhagia (Lippe)
